metadata.capability_extraction: Can select cell ranges in LibreOffice Calc and apply horizontal alignment using toolbar or Format menu. Demonstrated spreadsheet formatting capability.
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent ran out of steps trying to browse ACL Anthology for all four years of award data.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a formatting task: center-align header row A1:D1. Tests cell range selection and alignment formatting, which does not require any external web browsing.
metadata.explanation: The initial best_awards_acl.xlsx has default (left/general) alignment in row 1. Task asks agent to center-align A1:D1. Evaluator checks alignment.horizontal == 'center' for all four cells after save. Initial state fails because alignment is not 'center'. [Fixed: corrected func field to include check_ prefix; replaced truncated 8-char hash ab2cac09 with full 32-char MD5 7d3ab32fb77b1ea64cfabfdcd56b69aa computed from task_stem|variation_index]
fix_history: Fix 1: Added missing 'check_' prefix to evaluator.func (was 'xlsx_header_align__ab2cac09', now 'check_xlsx_header_align__7d3ab32fb77b1ea64cfabfdcd56b69aa')
Fix 2: Replaced invalid 8-char hash 'ab2cac09' with full 32-char MD5 '7d3ab32fb77b1ea64cfabfdcd56b69aa' in func, result.type, getter function name, and metric function name

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the xlsx file from the Docker environment via env.controller.get_file and uses openpyxl to extract cell alignment.
Column range (1-4, i.e. A:D) is appropriately hardcoded to match the expected 4-column file structure (title, year, author list, PDF link).
Metric correctly checks that all four header cells have horizontal alignment equal to 'center', matching the instruction's requirement.
Negative control resistance is sound: default/unmodified cells have alignment.horizontal == None (not 'center'), so the initial state correctly fails.
Postconfig saves the file via Ctrl+S before verification, ensuring the agent's changes are captured.
The evaluator.func field uses the corrected 32-char MD5 hash matching the actual function files; static validation found no current issues.
Minor: cell.alignment is never None in openpyxl (always an Alignment object), making the 'if cell.alignment else None' guard redundant but harmless.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider dynamically detecting the number of occupied columns in row 1 instead of hardcoding 4, to make the getter more robust to files with different column counts.
The 'if cell.alignment else None' guard can be simplified to just 'cell.alignment.horizontal' since openpyxl always returns an Alignment object.
